findings.change: Optional: register the selection-writing defer after the fix-record defer, so a failed write is seen before the fix record is stamped.
findings.claim: If the selection record cannot be written after a green run, test impact exits 1. But the lane-fix record (the 'fix' file) has already been stamped green by an earlier-running deferred function. The two records then disagree about the same run.
findings.evidence: Go runs deferred functions last-registered first. In cmd/metasystem/test_impact.go the selection writer's defer (around line 82) is registered before the plain.ReadFix/WriteFix defer (around line 106), so the fix record is written with CheckResult green first, and only then can the selection writer turn the exit code to 1. This needs a disk write failure in the check's own execution directory, which is rare. The slice works and is safe without a fix.

findings.change: None now. D2-U4, which reworks the repair cache, should have committedImpactCheck clear the variable or take the cache result directly instead of through the environment.
findings.claim: The hook is controlled only by the process environment. committedImpactCheck, used by work commit, runs test impact --check in the same process and then reads back repair-check.json. If that process ever had METASYSTEM_CHECK_SELECTION set, the cache would not be saved and the read-back would fail or pick up an older file. Today nothing reaches this: the variable is set only on the unit check's cheap process, and test impact removes it from the environment of every group it runs.
findings.evidence: test_impact.go line 37 reads os.Getenv through the sources struct, and line 126 skips the cache save when the path is set. committedImpactCheck at test_impact.go lines 627-636 reads repair-check.json after calling runTestImpactSelection. intent_work_commit.go line 219 is its only production caller. No traced path sets the variable in a work commit process.

findings.claim: With the path set and no base given, --publication-only now exits 1 on a git error, where it used to run. This cannot happen through UnitCheck: there --publication-only is the audits command, which is never given the path.
findings.evidence: test_impact.go lines 178-187 resolve the base for publication-only when the path is set. intent_unit_check.go line 95 and intent_carry_check.go line 76 use 'metasystem test impact --publication-only' as Audits, not as Cheap. unit_check.go line 132 adds the path for the cheap command only. The brief allows only a replay to record no base, so failing here is consistent with it.
